subject: Private deployment environment commissioning — circuit handover & credentials
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aerohealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment environment commissioning — circuit handover & credentials

Tom,

Thanks again for the run-through this morning. Attached are the circuit spec CSV and our high-level network diagram (see attachments). To keep the activation sprint tight, below are the minimal gating items we need confirmed before we open the staging window: 

- Physical circuit: provider handoff completed, carrier ASN + VLANs confirmed (attach: aerohealth-circuit-specs.csv)
- BGP peering endpoints + remote ASN: please confirm neighbor IPs and MD5 if used
- MTU and jumbo support on transit path (we recommend 9000 for model KV cache flows)
- Staging subnet allocation and sample IPs for our bastion/jumpbox
- Service account and service-account key rotation plan for Connector (we prefer short-lived keys + KMS-backed signing)
- KMS integration: do you have a customer-managed key in your KMS that we can reference? If not, we can propose a short-lived envelope flow
- Egress allowlist: provide the CIDR block(s) for temporary test egress and any upstream firewall contact

Proposed quick timeline: once items above are confirmed, Redwood will request a 2-hour staging window (recommended weekday after 17:00 local) for smoke traffic and BGP flap tests.

Doc links: I’ve uploaded a draft staging test plan and a DocuSign room for the circuit acceptance signatures: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d ; https://app.docusign.com/rooms/xyz123

Please reply with the circuit confirmation and any missing items — I’ll coordinate internal owners.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Senior Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: aerohealth-circuit-specs.csv, redwood-network-diagram-v1.pdf
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aerohealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: AeroHealth Network Ops <netops@aerohealth.com> , Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment environment commissioning — circuit handover & credentials

Laura —

Appreciate the checklist. Quick answers and a couple of follow-ups: 

1) Carrier handoff: confirmed. Carrier ASN 64512, VLANs 110/210. I attached the signed LoA to our internal ops thread (I'll forward if you need it).
2) BGP neighbor IPs: 10.250.10.2 (AeroHealth edge), remote neighbor 10.250.10.1 (Redwood). We currently do not use MD5 on the peering.
3) MTU: transit supports 9000 end-to-end.
4) Staging subnet: we can allocate 10.128.40.0/24 for staging. Jumpbox sample IP: 10.128.40.5.
5) KMS: AeroHealth uses Vault (self-hosted) with a customer-managed key; we will provide read-only policy for signing.
6) Egress: temporary egress allowlist confirmed — will provide CIDR and firewall contacts in my next email.

A few questions:
- For the service-account key rotation you mentioned, can Redwood accept short-lived tokens minted via our Vault OIDC flow?
- Do you require the LoA to show circuit L1 handoff before the staging window?

Thanks — Tom

Tom —

Thanks for the fast answers, that gets us most of the way there. Inline responses below.

> For the service-account key rotation you mentioned, can Redwood accept short-lived tokens minted via our Vault OIDC flow?

Yes — Redwood's Connector supports OIDC-issued short-lived tokens. We will need a service account with a role that can mint tokens scoped to the Connector's identity; scope and TTL we can coordinate. Ben, can you confirm the recommended TTL for Connector sessions?

> Do you require the LoA to show circuit L1 handoff before the staging window?

We do ask for carrier confirmation of physical handoff in the ticket. A scanned LoA or carrier portal screenshot is sufficient for scheduling staging. If there's any reason the carrier handoff might be delayed, flag it early and we'll adapt the date.

Next steps I propose:
- Tom: send firewall contact + egress CIDR (by EOD Friday)
- Ben: schedule a 2-hour staging window for the week of Oct 13 — preferred evening (18:00–20:00 PT).
- Karthik: I'll need a short list of acceptance smoke tests (BGP establish, prefix advertisement, 2-minute sustained 50 RPS traffic, KV cache warmup) so we can include in the runbook.

I’ve attached a short staging test plan (staging-test-plan.xlsx) to the Drive folder. DocuSign room is live for the circuit acceptance; please sign when ready.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: staging-test-plan.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment environment commissioning — circuit handover & credentials

Tom / Laura —

Technical notes for the staging window and acceptance tests: 

- BGP: we will establish eBGP with your ASN (64512). Please pre-configure the neighbor and confirm there is no route filtering that will drop our /24 advertisements. We will announce a test /24 from the staging block.
- MTU: confirm end-to-end 9000 (we will drop to 1500 if we detect fragmentation during smoke tests)
- NAT: avoid hairpin NAT on the staging subnet for jumpbox -> connector traffic; we need direct routing to observe KV cache/latency behavior.
- Time sync: ensure NTP reachability for staging hosts (our tests are time-sensitive for token TTLs)
- Maintenance window: proposed Oct 14, 18:00–20:00 PT. We require a two-hour continuous slot; please confirm by Oct 8.

I uploaded a short spreadsheet with the test sequence and expected outputs to the Drive folder (staging-test-plan.xlsx). Attaching as a stub here for visibility.

--
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: staging-test-plan.xlsx (stub)

Tom / team —

Confirming timeline and owners: 

- Tom: please send the egress CIDR and firewall POC by EOD Oct 8 (this is blocking our sign-off).
- Ben: I’ll mark Oct 14, 18:00–20:00 PT as tentative in our internal calendar and request the infra rotation with on-call.
- Laura: I’ll draft the smoke-test section for the runbook (BGP establish, prefix advertisement validation, 2-minute 50 RPS consumer traffic, KV cache warm-up and cold-cache tail latency check).

Security note: for the Vault-to-Connector flow, we’ll use ephemeral Vault tokens with a max TTL of 1 hour. Please confirm whether AeroHealth can support OIDC or if we need to fall back to an HSM-signed envelope.

Next sync: quick 20-minute call Wednesday with NetOps to finalize neighbor IPs and LoA. I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
